medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The University was founded on the principle that serious and sustained discourse among people of different faiths, cultures and beliefs promotes intellectual, ethical and spiritual understanding.  Consistent with this principle, the School of Medicine strives to ensure that its students become respectful physicians who embrace all dimensions of diversity in a learning environment that understands and includes the varied health care needs and growing diversity of the populations we serve.  The School of Medicine has a diverse student body, with students from groups underrepresented in medicine. Inquiries can be addressed to the Office of Diversity and Inclusion.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students wishing to interrupt their medical education for any reason must receive permission from the Committee on Students for a Leave of Absence. Leaves of Absence are granted for academic, medical, or compelling personal reasons pursuant to published policies.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are a wide variety of student organizations and interest groups ranging from Student Government to the Iron-Med Triathlon to specialty groups to faith-based organizations:  http://som.georgetown.edu/studentservices/groups/.  There is an annual Powder Puff football match between the first and second years.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located on the undergraduate campus in the heart of Georgetown, Our School of Medicine is next to MedStar Georgetown University Hospital.  The School of Medicine contains a health science library and an integrated learning center with 10 clinical examination rooms. Adjacent to the hospital is the Lombardi Cancer Center, which provides both research and clinical care. The School is near the NIH and other internationally prominent health care and research facilities. The Yates Field House offers swimming, jogging tracks, and other athletic programs. The Leavey Center hosts dining establishments and guest quarters.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Georgetown strives to be an inclusive community and to provide equal educational and employment opportunities for all. Individuals with disabilities may request reasonable accommodations that enable them to benefit from and participate fully in our academic, workplace and other environments, programs and activities.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Georgetown University School of Medicine is an institution rooted in the Catholic, Jesuit ideal of cura personalis, care of the whole person. As such, the School of Medicine is committed to creating and sustaining an educational environment that fosters the values and virtues of mutual respect, trust, honesty, collegiality, compassion, and accountability.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Medical students must travel throughout their four-year curriculum and are strongly recommended to have a driver's license and access to a vehicle. Particularly in the Foundational, Clinical, and Advanced Clinical Phases, students often face transportation challenges, as many care sites and hospitals are not easily accessible via public transport.  *If students do not have a license or vehicle, they are responsible for their own transportation.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to dress professionally for all patient interactions.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms:
In addition to the formal academic support provided by the course/module faculty and the Office of Medical Education, first
and second year students can participate in Peer-to-Peer Tutoring at no cost
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Variable; Lectures, small groups, team-based learning, workshops, case-based instruction, self-directed learning
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Scheduling allows students to put in quarterly preferences for site locations and services for core clinical clerkships; Students place preferences for fourth-year course requirements
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Promotes a longitudinal approach to training physicians. In the Foundational phase, students learn basic science and doctoring curricula through integrated, systems-based modules and longitudinal disciplines with exposure to normal and abnormal pathophysiology (16-month period). Training is complemented with robust simulated and live clinical educational experiences, early patient exposure, advocacy, & the ethical/cultural dimensions of medicine. The Core Clerkship Phase (Spring 2nd year) provides comprehensive clinical training in the care of patients through clerkships in the major-medical specialties. The Advanced Clinical Phase (summer 4th year) gives each student substantial responsibility for the management of patients through acting internships, elective study, and research. Extracurricular opportunities are available to students such as the longitudinal scholarly tracks (health justice, population health, literature & medicine, and more) as well as a Mind-Body Medicine Program and international rotations.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The School of Medicine curriculum provides an ethos of service and advocacy, stimulates a sense of community, and encourages a capacity for leadership among students that is directed towards the care of the most vulnerable, disenfranchised, and under-served in our society.  The service learning experience requires students to work in community-based, school-based, clinically based, or health policy programs. Student teams of 4-10 students are guided by faculty team leaders who relate these experiences to concepts taught in Health Disparities & Health Equity, Health Advocacy & Policy, and Community-Based Learning. Students choose to work in diverse environments, with Spanish speaking populations, women residents of shelters for survivors of domestic violence, children ages 5-12 in after-school programs providing instruction in health education, and in a non-profit health care agency dedicated to serving homeless and medically underinsured or uninsured populations.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: All students must complete an independent research project on a topic of interest to them.  Guided by a mentor, they may select topics as varied as medicine and law, medicine and business, medicine and ethics, or specific personal interests.  Students may elect to participate in five-year MD/MS or MD/MBA Programs or a seven-year MD/PhD Program.  Students may also pursue other professional degrees and/or research years prior to graduation.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students must complete a minimum of 20 hours by graduation.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The School of Medicine works in association with a wide variety of federal and community hospitals in the Washington, DC and Baltimore area.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/fail for pre-clinical curriculum; currently pass/fail for core clerkships; tiered (Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail) for advanced clinical phase

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded in 1851, Georgetown University School of Medicine has been committed to the pursuit of knowledge in the service of the community.  With a tradition of excellence in clinical education, Georgetown seeks to provide its students with a general professional education in medicine that integrates the scientific, clinical, and humanistic disciplines and lays the groundwork for the intellectual and ethical formation of physician-healers, committed to the clinically competent care of, and the well being of their patients.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Georgetown University School of Medicine is heir to the Jesuit traditions of care of the sick and commitment to service and social justice. The School embodies the university’s dedication to the pursuit of knowledge in service to others through excellence in clinical care, scientific discovery, and the formation of physician-healers.

The Georgetown medical experience is grounded in Cura Personalis, care for the whole person encompassing psychological, spiritual, social, and physical well-being. Within an environment integrating rigorous scientific inquiry and compassionate clinical practice, students develop the intellectual, ethical, and professional foundations required to become clinically excellent physicians, innovative scientists, and advocates for underserved communities.

Georgetown’s educational mission is strengthened by a culture of research and scholarship. Dual-degree opportunities, including MD-PhD programs in neuroscience, tumor biology, bioethics, and related biomedical sciences, prepare physician-scientists to advance discovery while improving patient care.

Clinical education occurs through Georgetown’s partnership with MedStar Health across diverse, high-acuity training environments including MedStar Georgetown University Hospital and MedStar Washington Hospital Center. Students gain experience in oncology, orthopedics, neuroscience, gastroenterology, trauma surgery, transplantation, and complex multidisciplinary care. The MedStar Georgetown Transplant Institute provides exposure to advanced multi-organ and intestinal transplantation and highly specialized medical and surgical care.

This rigorous clinical training fosters analytical thinking, sound clinical judgment, and evidence-based decision-making while emphasizing compassionate, whole-person care grounded in Jesuit values. Graduates emerge prepared to serve individual patients and advocate for communities with unmet healthcare needs.

Georgetown University School of Medicine seeks applicants committed to becoming physician-healers, scientists, and advocates. Service to the underserved remains central to the admissions philosophy and reflective of the Jesuit mission.

Independent Scholarly Project (ISP)
All medical students complete an Independent Scholarly Project (ISP), a mentored scholarly experience in which students investigate original questions across clinical, translational, educational, or basic science disciplines. The ISP strengthens skills in critical analysis, scientific communication, and evidence-based medicine while reinforcing Georgetown’s commitment to discovery in service of patient care.

Racial Justice Committee for Change (RJCC)
Guided by commitments to racial justice and health equity, Georgetown supports efforts to eliminate racism across the School of Medicine and medical center. The Racial Justice Committee for Change, composed of students, faculty, and staff, advances sustainable initiatives promoting equity and inclusion in medical education and healthcare delivery.

Curriculum
Georgetown’s holistic curriculum reflects its Catholic and Jesuit heritage and commitment to social justice. Critical thinking, cognitive integration, and lifelong learning guide curricular design. Cura Personalis unites longitudinal instruction in clinical skills, communication, ethics, and professional identity formation.

Community Service
Students complete a minimum of 20 hours of community service prior to graduation, reflecting Georgetown’s commitment to service and individualized attention to community needs beyond clinical training.

Student Life and Support Services
Located in Washington, D.C., Georgetown provides a dynamic environment supporting leadership, advocacy, and interdisciplinary collaboration while ensuring access to educational, spiritual, psychological, and medical resources that promote student well-being.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A minimum of one (1) committee letter/packet (required, if available) or two (2) individual letters is required.  There is a maximum of five (5) letters that can be submitted.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Invited candidates must attend a virtual presentation prior to the interview. These presentations are held on Mondays from mid-August- January, except holidays. Virtual interviews are scheduled Tuesday-Friday from September through February. Applicants receive one interview, conducted virtually, by a member of the basic science faculty, clinical faculty, or a selected fourth-year medical student.

Interviews last approximately 45 minutes and provide the Committee on Admissions with information on the applicant’s non-cognitive skills. Candidates are encouraged to discuss their unique background, motivation, interests, and goals during the interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews are one-on-one and conducted virtually.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: DACA recipients are eligible to apply.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: GUSOM accepts prerequisites completed at the community college level. In order to be competitive in the selection process, we encourage prospective applicants with community college prerequisites to supplement these courses by taking advanced courses in related subjects at their four year institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Prior to receiving an interview decision, applicants are permitted to submit post-submission corrections exclusively for the purpose of rectifying any errors within their original application. Following an interview, applicants are then eligible to submit post-submission updates. Finally, candidates placed on the waitlist may submit up to ten letters of interest.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Guided by the Jesuit tradition of cura personalis, care of the whole person, Georgetown University School of Medicine will educate a diverse student body, in an integrated way, to become knowledgeable, ethical, skillful, and compassionate physicians and biomedical scientists who are dedicated to the care of others and health needs of our society. An applicant for the M.D. degree, and an enrolled student seeking the M.D. degree, must meet the technical standards or functional equivalent, with or without reasonable accommodations, deemed essential functions for the care of patients.  These abilities and skills, as determined by Georgetown University School of Medicine, are: perception, communication, motor, intellectual-conceptual, integrative, and quantitative abilities, and behavioral and social attributes.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The school participates in federal financial aid programs and awards school-administered scholarships and low-interest loans to students on the basis of financial need. Parents' financial information is required for students seeking school-administered aid. Loan indebtedness counseling is an important function of the Office of Student Financial Planning, as a majority of students incur substantial educational debt. Candidates for admission are strongly encouraged to contact the office with questions.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Students who leave the School of Medicine prior to the end of the semester for any reason (withdrawal, leave of absence, dismissal) will receive refunds of tuition and fees according to the official policy.  Before officially withdrawing, students are advised to consult the Financial Aid Office for more information on the financial implications of your decision.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Academic requirements for admissions to the School of Medicine include adequate preparation in physics, biology, chemistry, mathematics, and English.  No application will be considered unless the applicant has completed 90 credit hours of course work at the time of application.  

It is strongly recommended to complete a biochemistry course, which can be substituted for Organic Chemistry II.

Advanced placement (AP) courses may fulfill the course requirements if the credits appear on the applicant's college or university transcript.  Applicants who were exempted from undergraduate English or math courses without credit may petition the Committee on Admissions in writing to waive the required credit hours. 

Questions regarding the eligibility of specific courses for meeting these requirements should be addressed to the Office of Admissions.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Committee on Admissions selects students on the basis of academic achievement, character, maturity, and motivation. The committee evaluates the applicant's entire academic record, performance on the MCAT, college premedical committee evaluations or letters of recommendation, personal essays, and personal interview. A secondary application and essay are required of all applicants. An applicant may be invited to interview once all credentials have been reviewed by the committee. The personal interview is required and conducted on the medical center campus. The School of Medicine does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, creed, age, disability, sexual orientation, or national or ethnic origin.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Substantive, longitudinal clinical experiences such as: shadowing a physician, medical mission trips, scribing, community EMS, etc.  Please note that volunteering in clinic/waiting rooms such as playing/reading to children, stocking shelves, and transporting patients is considered good volunteer experience, but is not hands-on clinical experience.  International experiences are acceptable, but a majority should be in the United States.
